notes: Customer priority: full Private (VPC) deploy inside AWS account w/ strict egress controls.

- In-transit: mutual TLS enforced for all inter-service traffic; client certs stored in customer CA; Redwood must support mTLS termination in customer subnet or present client cert to internal services.
- At-rest: must be AES-256 encrypted, all model KV caches and user-provided artifacts stored on EBS with encryption-by-default; DB snapshots encrypted.
- Key management: BYOK required. Customer uses AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed CMKs and requires Redwood to integrate via Grant/Encrypt APIs without exporting key material.

- Key rotation: policy = automatic rotation every 90 days; requirement to demonstrate zero-downtime key rollover for ongoing KV cache and token decrypts; rotation flow must be documented and validated in POC.

- Secrets management: customer uses HashiCorp Vault for secrets and dynamic DB credentials. Redwood must support retrieving secrets via Vault (AppRole) or accept short-lived signed certs; no long-lived plaintext secrets in config.

- Audit & telemetry: all access and admin operations must be forwarded to company SIEM; Redwood audit logs must include key usage events, encrypted in transit to syslog endpoint; retention requested = 7 years for legal/compliance team.
- Data residency: production datasets must remain in us-east-1; logical separation per business unit; subprocessor list and SOC2 Type II artifact required prior to procurement.

- Network & routing: egress lock-down via AWS NACLs and Security Groups, private endpoints to Redwood control plane, optional S3 VPC endpoints for model artifacts; strong preference for direct peering or Transit Gateway attachments.
- 2-week POC to prove: 1) KMS BYOK grant lifecycle, 2) mTLS handshake with client cert rotation, 3) Vault-based secret injection, 4) audit log forwarding to Splunk endpoint.
- Performance constraints for POC: p95 latency <= 200ms for 256-token chat, throughput target 500 req/min with <5% degradation when KV cache hot.
